## Part I: The Confession of the Flame

Oftentimes I sabotaged myself, and I knew exactly why: I wanted peace and clarity away from everyone else around me. I wanted to be alone, far from all this noise and chaos. And so, I self-sabotaged again, stabbing and piercing that knife right through my own heart. Why, though? How could I do it to myself this time?

Life has been great - amazing, even. I've found another way of living. I remember the advice to seek healing through counseling and talking, the warnings about how opening up would free me from myself, and the long discussions about the little things that could trigger the rage and anger I suppressed through all those years of enduring. I know I spoke ill back then, but I am well now. In fact, I feel great. Empowered. I have allowed myself to not only have friends but to truly love and appreciate them. Here we are, feeling lighter than a dandelion floating across a field after a light breeze.

I have about five friends now. They are remarkable individuals in their fields, full of prospect.

There is Natalie, whom I met in my first year at Wits. It turned out we liked almost the same things: chess, brunch, vintage living, and romanticizing life. A little tea party held in a wonderful garden during spring is our favorite excuse to dress up and alter our accents to sound British enough for time travel. She is marvelous. Once, she retook a calculus class just because she didn't get the exact perfect marks she wanted, even though she had already passed. It's the ultimate perfectionist move, and I absolutely loved it. To me, it resembled how free she thinks of herself; she won't let something slide if she has the power to change it.

Then there is Starborn, whom I met around my year of serious rebellion. We had so much fun. Back then, I still thought of myself as daddy's princess, living in a bubble despite an environment that never missed a beat to remind me otherwise. Physically, I was living in a pit hole - deep inside a crusted, rough city, in the heart of a forgotten, decaying building. I hated everything about that place: the dusty hallways, the unreliable elevator, the odd-smelling corridors that made it difficult to escape to my imaginary tea parties in London.There were times I thought about just going on a quest to find the next man willing to take me into his castle and let me feast on his life's work. It wasn't the deed itself that was hard, just the thought of the mental strength and rebellion it would take to achieve it. I failed dismally in each of those mental quests. Maybe it was because of my hot-headedness and my total unwillingness to bend to a man's will. I don't intend to scrutinize my former self too deeply; it would kill my spirit to dissect her like that.

## Part II: The Echoes of Envy

Then there are the others. Starborn's rebound friend - someone I barely knew - evoked resounding feelings in me that pushed me in a contrary direction. Perhaps she reminded me of the relationship I never had with my mother, or the one I wished I had. She unknowingly amplified the parts of myself I had buried instead of facing, the parts I hid instead of letting the sun burn the living hurt out of them. I had to come to terms with the fact that my envious friction had little to do with her; she was just an entity representing the pieces of myself I hadn't tapped into yet.

But that doesn't exempt her from my genuine dislike of how she chose to scrutinize my expression. I remember posting a photo on Instagram - me sitting at a bar with my friend Pixie, wearing a black fitted mesh jumpsuit, a floral scarf framing my face, minimal but seductive makeup, long boots, and a fur coat just out of frame. The mood was warm, cozy, nightlife. She saw it and decided to use it as gossip fuel for Starborn, bashing it, saying I needed to "tone it down, i'm doing too much," that it was "too revealing" and "inappropriate for Instagram." Well, congratulations to the Minister of Moral Dressing. Kudos on becoming the monarchy of social media modesty. I just think if you're going to critique my clothes, you should do it to my face. I am an easy person to critique; I won't cry, and I won't break. I look for the truth in what people say, and I speak my truth back, whether it displeases them or not. I choose what offends me through reasoning and validity. If someone says something hurtful but true, I can calmly say, "I hear you, that makes sense," and move on. But the two-faced energy around her was impossible to ignore.

## Part III: The Poison in the Text

The one I won't mention is slightly astounding. She struck right when I least expected it and used a poison I thought she did not possess. She gave me the best smackdown and ultimate trash on why you should never let your guard down. Talk about returning to campus after a very lovely holiday in Cape Town. It was around dinner time at home. My dad had just finished making our dinner, and we were going to sit down and enjoy that with one of those political debates he likes. As I sat on the couch trying to settle myself comfortably, my phone vibrates… trtrtrtr. It's a message from Starborn. I feel a bit lazy and reluctant to check because I know it will turn into a long conversation of us debriefing the holiday and just having a good laugh. I think to myself, let me enjoy my steak and mash; I will give her a call before I go to bed. My dad comes and gives me my food. Before I could taste another bite, texts come through… trtrtr. Okay, now I have to check, because two texts in less than a minute signal it is really good tea that just cannot wait for the daily debrief hour before bed.I'm on my phone now. As I click to read the message, an astounding, impossible rock hits my chest. The text goes like:

"Hey, have you ever had a fight/altercation with Ponani?"
The next one is just a dying need for a response:
"???"
I reply with a nice:
"Not at all, why?" 
 
She tries texting back and decides no, she has to call for this one. My phone rings, so I get up and make my way to my room with my food, signaling to my dad that I have to take the call. After about an hour of multiple unexpected shocks - bricks and cement of impossible, revolting scenarios and ultimate, disturbing shocks about me - I turn cold. I'm in awe; I'm shocked to the ultimate core. You could tell me the worst shocking news, no matter how awful and sad, and I still wouldn't get past that level of shock. I was cognitively, psychologically, and emotionally paralyzed. Like, what in the living hell was she trying to accomplish?
I switch off my phone, eat my food, and prepare for bed. My whole body and soul were in complete denial, like there is absolutely no way on earth that Starborn was telling it as it is. I had to be in Joburg the next few days to digest this in person. The next few days in Cape Town, I was just out of my body, trying to get past each day. I did think of telling this to someone, maybe my dad, but I don't know how to do that. I never talk to my dad about anything, let alone my mother. Even though my dad is way closer to my heart, I still have never confided in him about anything that was not a joke. 

## Part IV: The Confrontation and the Crisis

My first day in Joburg, I had to have brunch by Bannister, and I saw you walking past. You did not realize my presence in the area, nor did I intend to make you aware. Moments of being glad I'm back and seeing Starborn passed, and I wanted to know exactly what was going on.She was extremely reluctant at first, completely detached from wanting to tell me all this, which puzzled me because when mountains separated us, she jumped quickly on that call. The atmosphere was heavy; I could tell she was weighing the validity of these allegations, and she was also confused and just trying to look out for her best interest. I was not playing either; I wanted to know at any cost.She first says I should ask Ponani myself and that she doesn't want to get in between. I'm taken aback, feeling stripped of my innocence by the second. I make it easy:
"I know you and understand why you are holding back, but I want you to know I don't appreciate it. You can always keep your distance from me to protect yourself if you feel like doing so, but you have to tell me exactly what it is she said about me. Me and you have been friends for so long, and I never gave you any reason to doubt me, nor have you given me one. However, you holding back on telling me to my face everything Ponani had the highest audacity to say about me is not shining a better light on you."
I was hurt, deeply wounded at that point, and I know I was putting pressure on her, but I did not care. Because you know what? If anything was being said about her, I would tell her straight from the moment I heard it. I continued to make it known that anyone who knew about this and did not tell me is not really a true friend to me, and God as my witness, I will unfriend them. I was not joking at all, and I think she also realized that much.

We go to the Freshers party; we are dressed and look all cute. Pixie is also there, and we are pregaming. I am pulled together, and my emotions are all in check. We start at Bannister, take a few shots each, get some really cute photos, and then make our way to the party. It was lit; it was nice and vibey with good music and good people. That was my first time at Freshers, and I was loving every bit of it until… I got drunk. The alcohol kicked in and did its best to amplify my feelings. Now I was in a disinhibited state, and my raw, unprocessed feelings were racing each other to the surface. The raw, unprocessed, and unfiltered Challotte was out. I was mad. Autopilot was over; I was enraged more than I could comprehend. I started weeping, and they later told me that I kept saying, "Why me? Like, how could she do me like that?" I kept rehearsing each and every one of her accusations.

I think I was only doing so in my head, but who knows, I might have said one or two out loud. 
I'm thinking to myself:

1. She claims that her guru told her that she is having insomnia and struggling to focus on her schoolwork and perform her best  because someone is after her intellectual property.
2. The person is intensely after her and her life's prospects.
3. The same person has been using a technique called "knowledge swapping," and she has been practicing the aforementioned method for years, and that is how they got through prior stages of their life.
4. The person does not belong at Wits; they lack the cognitive functioning that a Wits candidate needs to get through. The person is not smart or intellectually gifted at all; they are just a fraud who gets by by preying on individuals such as her.
5. She tells Starborn to be extremely cautious around my presence because I am this entity that is assigned by dark powers to perform these dark assignments on her, and therefore Starborn should be vigilant because I am extremely dangerous and witchy.
6. She says because I sometimes watch Shera Seven, the "sprinkle sprinkle" lady, I perform dark magic.
7. She claims now I am after her whole family, and they all cannot live in harmony and peace and be prosperous on earth because I want harm their way.

I go on and on in my head. At this point, I myself am extremely puzzled. Shera Seven talks about a gold-digging lifestyle, so what does that have to do with all this nonsense? If I was able to perform knowledge swapping, wouldn't I just utilize that power by swapping knowledge at the bank and getting richer? I'm perplexed. If I was so powerful as she claims, why would I waste my power on lower forms like that instead of doing worthwhile things, becoming more blessed financially, and having absolutely no need for a degree? If I possessed such power, I wouldn't be using it to swap useless university knowledge I can get on a YouTube video; I would do next-level stuff. 
I realized that I am getting more pissed by each and every one of these allegations because they have no stance whatsoever. She wants to tell me about not belonging at Wits? Missy, I turned down UCT, remember? I got into UCT and you did not. Who did I switch my knowledge with in high school then? Oh no, what about primary school? You go to my mountain collection of awards, medals, and certificates that date back from kindergarten, and you want to say I switched knowledge with a kindergarten kid on how to do my ABCs? 
Now I'm thinking maybe she is envious that she studied all the time and I would go out, come back, and study a semester's worth of work in two days and still be above average. If that was it, did she miss the fact that even then, I was not doing as well as I did in first year? I got above average because I did use to do some studying here and there along the semester, and just because I did not tell her doesn't mean I did not do it. I'm thinking, so for a full 2 to 3 months I used to see her at school, and the times I used to request to shower at her res (which was a communal shower, by the way, when my building did not have power), she was looking at me with dark eyes and thinking I'm there to poison her life's work… I was feeling so shut out. Like, wtf, all these times we all used to chill, she was tiptoeing around me and thinking to herself, "Emihle is so dark, she is the reason I take drugs to sleep now and can't get above average even though I studied." What a bitch! I had to address her.

## Part V: Guarding the Name

I saw her the other day as I was making my way to campus. I had confided in my aunt on the phone the night before and had a very good cry. She reminded me that this has nothing to do with me and I shouldn't doubt myself, because I was starting to do so. I had started doubting my capabilities and why God made me like this. Why do I seem to have people want to treat me well? Why do I seem to make some people at ease and some not at ease? I had started debugging how I do it - how I learn that much content in two days and still pass. Like, is there something I am not aware of that keeps helping me? I had started trying to believe the most shameful things being said about me. I wanted to at least see some tiny bit of truth so I could understand why she would go to such lengths trying to discredit who I am. She made it her mission, so I came to realize, that she had diffused this narrative about me to almost everyone whom I knew that she also knew. Some she knew through me, but she made sure everyone saw me as the biggest villain of all time. Witchcraft is not something black groups take lightly. She nailed the last nail in the coffin when she validated her claims by saying she went to a spiritual leader (a prophet or whatever), and she knew most of the people she told would take it very seriously and be extremely shaken because they were black. Imagine laughing and talking to someone and not realizing that they are being fed the most villainizing poison about you, and they are also just trying not to be your next victim. Imagine walking around and people are thinking such things about you - maybe she's walking that fast to practice her next spell, or look at how she's dressed all in black today, it must be the day of the ritual… A whole 2 to 3 months of some of my mates thinking all that about me, and I couldn't even tell. I was beat, shamed, and ultimately left for dead.

I thought about being the bigger person and just taking it in because I know the truth and time will later show her it was not me. BUT I recalled The 48 Laws of Power, Law 5:
"So much depends on reputation - guard it with your life.''

I had to do something about this. I cannot let her slide. I did a bit of research online and figured she is tarnishing my reputation at this point. Her not liking me is okay, but diffusing such shameful things about me around the people I hang around is an active attempt at ruining my reputation. I walked up to them, and she was with someone. I called her to the side and asked for a quick chat. Talk about extreme pretense when they see me - all smiles and attempting to hug, asking, "How are you?" I was amused at how long she was planning to keep it rolling. I asked her to the side and quickly sum it all up for me: what is it that she has been actively diffusing about me, and why? She couldn't come up with a definite answer. I proceeded by telling her that I am not interested in going back-and-forth with this; let's just do a lie detector test. I told her, "You can find the place, time, and the person, and I am going to cover the costs no matter how much they are." I was very assured in myself at that time, and I wanted her to know that was the last straw. She said things that were not making sense and denied some of the things she supposedly said. I told her, "Sweetheart, if you do not like me, that is okay. I do not have to like you either. But if you want to have this battle with me, let's do it the legal way. Bring the person who said all that to the court, we do some lie detector tests to please everyone, and clear my name from all this so you can know that I am not after you, nor will I ever be." She suddenly became a bit reluctant and focused on denying, and then I proceeded again to let her know that I will sue her for defamation of character should I sense that she has not stopped, and then I left.


Being you is not easy, and maybe that is what forms you the way you are, really. To truly process all of this, I had to do some serious self-reflection, dating it all back from the earlier life moments until now. I wrote something for you just after i learned all this; maybe I thought it would provide some clarity, understanding, and a bit of comfort in such times….

2 days I don't feel

Two days, and I don't feel.
Two days after, and I still don't know.
I don't know what it is about me - 
It's like a torch that won't burn out,
It's like a rose that won't decay,
A route that won't delay.

Persistent, it won't let go.
Dedicated, it won't stop showing.
Consistent, it vowed to be what it's been - 
No motivation needed for it to be.

I tried dimming it so it won't be seen,
Dimmed it again and again so it's dim.
"Dim it for me," I thought, "so they won't see."
Dim it is, but still, they could see - 
A little light across the sea,
Far, but close enough to be seen.

One saw it.
Two conspired about it.
Three… it probably reached more than that.

Just one loyalty it needed:
A person who will believe in it more than I,
A person who will rescue it, not hide it like I.

It reached…
She did.

The thing is, she didn't understand what it is.
Sometimes it poses as a threat, but it's not.
At times it is a mess.
She misjudged it, left my existence for dead.
Because it is mine, she had but one deed:
Consult. Consult me on what it is.

And I could tell her:
It is a Star.

Bury it today, it will live.
Come back tomorrow, it will breathe.
You can't kill it,
Nor dim it.
I tried.
Ask my past offenders - it won't die.
It will live.
It is MyStar.

# You do not love me

You do not love me.

You do not even know me, let alone try to.
You have no intention of seeing me beyond the surface.

You plan not to tour the scars,
the lies
those that lie beneath the surface you experience first.

You want the lie,
spot the lie,
quickly construct a mere conclusion
of that which you have not known.

You do not love me.

You have no desire to give more of your time
to see me through my own eyes,
right through the depths and hopes of my soul.
You have no desire to stare past my siren eyes,
see no lust,
no sexual nature,
but more of what constructs them like so.

You want surface.

Transaction.

A barren bowl,
that which could hold your experiences,
remember all about you like memory
except it is in human form,
very warm,
and could fulfill the things you cannot.

You do not love me.

You do not want to love me.
You have no desire to learn to want me.
You do not yearn to know me past this horizon.

You just want a companion
to carry your cross with.

You want

not to die of cold in winter,
not to die of ill-prepared hunger combats.

You want a business-like partnership from me.

You say,
I will do this,
and you do that,
like that is all it should ever be.

If you loved me,
I would know.

You would hold me
like you were trying to learn me,
studying an ancient book
you have been yearning to digest for decades.
The ins and outs of my breath
would be elements that excite you.
You would gaze not into my eyes,
but straight to my depths.
Deep,
deep,
deep
way beyond those blooded veins.

You would see that window to the soul,
carefully constructed as siren eyes.
Even when you do get swept off your feet,
deeply empowered by sexual desires,
you would do so to me
as you would wish to do internal.

If you loved me,
you would see me as more than just,
and more of all.
You would want to do for me.
Learn my paths.
Trace my content
from origin to now.
You would not want to be good with me,
but exceptional to me.

Memorize my ways of living
so you know me beneath and above.
You would want to learn my impulse,
what I possess
when possessed alone.

You would want to know me
just like I think I know me.

You would want to understand
the dilation of my pupils
to know when I am taken aback in awe,
and when I am in danger.

You would carefully construct
your spirit animal to align with mine,
or mine with yours,
to not only wish to protect me in flesh,
but also in there—
that which we still yearn
to fully experience.

You would want to intertwine with me,
not only in flesh,
but more so in the highest dimensions,
higher planes,
higher consciousness.

You would claim me
before this world
and the next.

# Scars

Tracked,
through the wound to remind me what i've seen.

There..
always hidden. 
A part always beaten.

I've seen the best, worst 
Not only them all, but all sometimes i couldnt show.

I've tried hidding it,
it gets worse everytime i do so.

They said it needs the wind to brush
eat, run through them trying to dry all that moisture 
Moisture that servers as reminder of how painful it all was.

Scars i love that you are there and don't want you to fade.

I am afraid.. Soo scared..

what if someday you heal?
evapourate and i could nor longer feel you?

how will i remember, remember all that you came by with?

# Where the Light Forgot Me

*By Inathi Booi*

## Dedication

To the version of me who kept breathing through the ache. To the child who sat in silence hoping someone would notice. To the teenager who kept giving love even when none was returned. To the young woman I am now still healing, still here. And to anyone who's ever felt invisible, unchosen, forgotten. This book is a mirror. I see you. I feel you. You're not alone anymore.

## Opening Quote

"Some of us weren't just broken... we were forgotten by the light itself.
But even in the dark, we learned to glow.”

# Where the Light Forgot Me

I don't remember the exact moment the light stopped showing up for me. I just know one
day, I woke up, and it was gone. People always ask, “What happened to you? " like
sadness has a switch, like I can trace my darkness to one clear explosion. But it wasn't
one thing. It was everything, too many little breaks in the glass until I could no
longer see the sun through it. This is not a story of survival. It’s a confession. A
letter I never had the courage to write until now. Because maybe, just maybe, if I tell
it all... the light will find me again.

## Chapter 1 — The Girl Who Went Quiet

I used to talk a lot. I used to laugh until my stomach hurt. I used to dream too big and love too loudly. But people taught me to shrink. At home, I learned to keep still. Not because I wanted to, but because silence was safer. The less they noticed me, the less they could break me. I would sit in corners, blending into walls, pretending to be fine. At school, I became a shadow. People liked the version of me that smiled on command and kept her emotions locked in a cage. They liked me quiet. So I stayed quiet. And slowly, I started disappearing from my own life.

## Chapter 2 — I Wasn't Always This Cold

Sometimes I look in the mirror and don't recognize the girl staring back. She looks numb. Unbothered. Like nothing can shake her. But I know her secret. I know she cries when everyone is asleep. I know she carries old words like they're written into her skin. I know she used to care too much until caring started to feel like bleeding. You don't become cold for no reason. You learn it. You become it. Because when you're too soft for too long, life shows you why that’s dangerous. I remember the days I begged the sky to give me a sign. That maybe someone, somewhere, still cared. But nothing ever came. And I started to believe what I feared most: that this world had no light left for girls like me.

## Chapter 3 — I Started Writing to Survive

Nobody noticed I was falling, so I started writing letters. Not to anyone in particular, just to the air, to the wind, to the space between me and the people I couldn't talk to. I wrote about the emptiness that kept showing up uninvited. About the way I could be surrounded by people and still feel like I was screaming in a room full of silence. About how tired I was of pretending I was okay just to keep others comfortable. And every time I finished a letter, I would hide it. In library books. Under my bed. Taped inside the back of an old notebook. Some part of me hoped someone might find them. The other part knew no one would. But I kept writing anyway. Because writing was the only thing that felt like breathing.

## Chapter 4 — The Day I Broke Without Making a Sound

It wasn't a big event. No dramatic breakdown. It was just a quiet Tuesday, and I couldn't get out of bed. The air felt heavy. The walls too close. I didn't cry—I couldn't. I just lay there, staring at the ceiling like it held all the answers. That’s when I realized I had become so used to surviving that I forgot what it felt like to live. And maybe that's what this whole story is about. Not dying. Not healing. But remembering. Remembering who I used to be, before the light forgot me.

## Chapter 5 — Home Isn't Always a Safe Place

People think “home” means comfort, warmth, safety. But I know different. I know that sometimes, home is where the pain lives. At home, I learned how to stay quiet when I wanted to scream. I learned how to carry my feelings in silence, because saying them out loud didn't change anything—it only made them worse. It's weird how a place can have your name on it, but still not feel like yours. How you can sit in a room full of your own blood, and still feel like you don't belong. Sometimes I'd go into the bathroom, close the door, and sit on the floor just to feel alone in peace. Because even the noise of people who are supposed to love you can become unbearable when it’s filled with judgment, pressure, or coldness. I wanted to leave. Not to run away—just to breathe somewhere new. Somewhere the walls didn’t remember every version of me that broke.

## Chapter 6 — I Started Faking It Better

There's an art to pretending you're okay. You smile just right. You laugh at the right moments. You post things that make it seem like you're still holding it together. I became so good at faking it, even I started to believe it sometimes. But it’s tiring. Pretending is its own kind of grief—you're mourning a version of yourself that never existed, just to survive the day. People would say, “You’re so strong,” and I'd smile, knowing damn well they had no idea I cried myself to sleep the night before. You get tired of carrying yourself like a lie. But when you don't feel safe enough to be honest, what choice do you have?

## Chapter 7 — I Started Wanting Less

I stopped asking for love. Stopped expecting people to understand me. Stopped believing that anyone would ever choose me and mean it. It wasn't bitterness—it was exhaustion. I started to want less. From people. From life. From myself. I didn't need big dreams anymore. Just peace. Not even happiness—just silence. A moment where I didn’t feel like the world was sitting on my chest. And I know that sounds dramatic, but when you carry too much for too long, even breathing feels like work.

## Chapter 8 — When the Light Showed Up, I Didn't Trust It

Something strange happened. One day, the light peeked through. Not a full sunrise—just a soft glow. A moment. A conversation. A song that made me feel again. But I didn't trust it. Because when you've lived in the dark for too long, light doesn't feel safe—it feels suspicious. You start waiting for it to disappear again. You brace yourself for the crash. You don't even let yourself enjoy it because you know nothing good stays. And maybe that’s the saddest part of all: I forgot how to hold joy without shaking.

## Chapter 9 — Where It All Began

It all started when I was seven. Not with a funeral. Not with screams or sirens. Just a moment. A feeling. A sudden silence inside me where something used to live. I lost a part of me that day. And I’ve been trying to remember what it felt like to be whole ever since. Maybe that’s when I forgot how to hold still without shaking. How to sit in a room without feeling like I didn't belong there. How to speak without wondering if anyone was really listening. That kind of pain doesn’t need a name. It doesn't ask for permission. It just... settles inside you. And grows. Everyone else kept moving forward—laughing, living, forgetting. But I stayed stuck in that seven-year-old body. Watching people through a glass I couldn't break. I didn't know how to say it then. I still don't, really. But I think that's the moment the light forgot me.

## Chapter 10 — The Invisible Room

Have you ever thought that maybe the hardest part of pain isn't the pain itself, but the way it makes you feel so completely alone—even when you are surrounded by people? It’s like existing in an invisible room, one that no one else sees. You can wave. Smile. Nod at the right moments. But deep down, you're hoping someone will see through the glass. I tried. I tried to speak, to write, to show it through my eyes. But pain is tricky—it teaches you to hide. So I did. And the more I hid, the more they thought I was okay. And the more they thought I was okay, the more I forgot how to ask for help. Now I'm eighteen. And I’ve mastered the art of losing people. Friends. Lovers. Even parts of myself. Not because I wanted to—because I didn’t know how to hold on. My anxiety walks into every room before I do. My overthinking writes endings to relationships that haven't even started. And still, I show up. Even when it hurts. Even when I want to disappear. Because deep down, some stubborn piece of me still believes the light will remember me one day. And until then, I write. I bleed on pages. I try to turn pain into something softer. Because maybe that’s what healing is—finding beauty in the places that broke you.

## Chapter 11 — The Day I Faded in a Crowd

There was this one day. I remember it like a bruise you keep pressing, just to feel something. I was standing in a crowded room. Loud voices. Laughter. Movement. And I had never felt more invisible. I smiled when someone looked at me. I laughed at the jokes I didn’t hear. I nodded like I was present—but I wasn't. I was floating just above the moment, watching it all unfold like a movie I couldn't step into. And it hit me. I could be in a room full of people and still feel like a ghost. That was the kind of loneliness no one talks about. Not the "I have no friends" kind. The kind where you do have them, but still feel alone. Still feel misunderstood. Still feel like no one would notice if you disappeared. And in that moment, something inside me cracked. Not loudly. Not enough for anyone to hear. Just enough for me to feel it. But instead of falling apart in front of everyone, I walked away. Went to the bathroom. Shut the door. Sat on the floor. And I cried without a sound. Because sometimes, you don't need comfort. You just need to let the sadness move through you. You just need to break without explaining. That day, I realized: It’s not always the loud breakdowns that matter. Sometimes it’s the quiet ones that stay with you the longest.

## Chapter 12 — When It Rains Inside

Some days, it feels like it's raining inside my body. Like there's a storm I carry with me that no one else can see. I wake up heavy. Not tired—exhausted. From the weight of pretending. Of functioning. Of carrying questions that don't have answers. Why do I feel this way? Why can't I just be happy like everyone else? Why does joy feel so temporary, and pain feel like home? I drag myself through the hours like I’m underwater. Smiling when I should. Laughing on cue. But everything sounds distant. Filtered through clouds. People say, "It'll pass." But what if it doesn't? What if I've made a home in the darkness? What if the light forgot me for real? Still—I get out of bed. Still—I brush my teeth. Still—I put on music, even if I don’t feel it. Because sometimes survival isn't poetic. Sometimes it’s just habit. And that has to be enough.

## Chapter 13 — The Almosts

My life is full of almosts. Almost happy. Almost healed. Almost loved. Almost enough. I almost made it out of that sadness last year. I almost opened up to that one person who made me feel seen. I almost believed I was okay. But the thing about almosts—they haunt you. They keep you up at night replaying what could have been. Sometimes I wonder if I’m cursed to live a life of nearlies. To always reach, but never touch. I meet people who almost stay. I get better—almost. I let someone in—almost. But then fear walks in, like it owns the place. And I go back to being quiet. Guarded. Alone. I'm tired of almosts. But they're the only thing I've known. So maybe I'll learn to live with them. Until I finally find something that stays.

## Chapter 14 — The Kindness I Needed

It wasn't a grand gesture. It never is. It was just a text: “Hey, I was thinking about you. Are you okay?” That message broke something in me. Not in a painful way. In a freeing way. Like someone finally opened the window in a dark room. It reminded me that sometimes, we survive on the smallest pieces of kindness. A touch on the shoulder. A smile that lingers. A person who stays when you're quiet. That day, I didn’t say much. I didn’t know how to let people into the mess inside me. But they didn't leave. They sat there. Waited. Let me breathe. And for the first time in a long time, I didn't feel broken. I felt human. Not fixed. Not saved. Just... not alone. And maybe that’s where healing begins. Not in huge moments. But in the gentle ones.

## Chapter 15 — The Light Isn't Gone

Some nights, the darkness still whispers. But now, I whisper back. I tell it: “I’m still here.” Not stronger. Not healed. Just still.

## Chapter 16 — The Smile I Wear

People say I smile a lot. They think it's a good thing. They call me strong. Brave. But they don't know it’s not bravery—it's survival. Every smile is stitched with silence. Every laugh, a distraction. Because if I stopped smiling, if I let the pain slip out—I might not stop crying. So I smile in the mirror to remind myself I’m still here. I smile for others so they don't ask questions I can’t answer. But beneath that smile is a war. A storm I never chose to fight. And some days, I don't even know who's winning.

## Chapter 17 — When Overthinking Becomes a Voice

You ever try to fall asleep, and your thoughts start sprinting? Like they’ve been waiting all day for the lights to go off. “What if they don't actually like you?” “What if you said too much again?” “What if you're just... too much?” My mind talks louder than anyone else in the room. It replays old conversations. Writes scripts for moments that haven't even happened. It's exhausting. To be at war with your own head. To want peace, but your brain won't give it to you. I wish I could turn it off. Even just for a night. But until then, I learn to live with the noise. To breathe through the static. To remind myself that just because my mind says it, doesn't mean it’s true.

## Chapter 18 — Ghosting Myself

I've ghosted people. But more than that—I've ghosted parts of me. The child who used to laugh without reason. The teen who believed in love. The version of me that thought I'd be okay by now. I left them behind because it was easier than facing what they became. But sometimes I hear them. In music. In memories. In moments of quiet. They're still there. Waiting. Maybe one day, I'll meet them again. Not with shame. But with grace.

## Chapter 19 — A Letter I Never Sent

Dear Me,

I'm sorry. I’m sorry for all the times I ignored you. For pretending you were okay when you weren't. For being kinder to others than I was to you. I know you're tired.

I know you feel forgotten. But you're still here. And that means something. You've survived every dark thought. Every long night.

Every goodbye you didn't understand. You are not weak. You are not a burden. You are not too much. You are a story still unfolding.

And maybe, just maybe, you're not as alone as you think.

Love, Me

## Chapter 20 — Cracks in the Shell

Some people see confidence and think it means you're fine. But they don't see the cracks under the surface. The way I second-guess every word after it's spoken. The way I shrink in loud rooms, even while smiling. They don't know that I talk to myself in the mirror. Just to stay sane. “Breathe. You're okay. You're safe.” Because sometimes the only voice that comforts me—is my own.

## Chapter 21 — Things I Never Say Out Loud

Sometimes, I want to scream. Not at anyone in particular. Just... into the air. Just to remind myself I still have a voice. I want to say, “I’m not okay.” I want to say, “Please stay.” I want to say, “Love me even when I pull away.” But I don't. Because I don't want to sound weak. I don’t want to be a burden. So I stay silent. And it eats me from the inside out.

## Chapter 22 — The Room with No Door

Sometimes, it feels like I’m trapped in a room with no door. Just walls made of memories and ceilings of regret. No way out. No way forward. Just the echo of my own thoughts. But even then—I find a pen. And I write on the walls. Because if I can’t leave the room, maybe I can change what's inside it.

## Chapter 23 — Quiet Victories

Getting out of bed. Replying to a text. Looking in the mirror and not turning away. These are victories. Quiet ones. Uncelebrated ones. But real. Some days, survival is the achievement. And that’s enough.

## Chapter 24 — The Friend Who Stayed

Not everyone leaves. Some stay. Some see through the silence and sit in it with you. There was one. They didn't try to fix me. They just held space for me. And that was enough. Sometimes, presence is the only thing that heals.

## Chapter 25 — If I Could Talk to 7-Year-Old Me

I’d tell her, You're not broken. You're not too sensitive. You're not too much. You're just feeling what others refuse to feel. You're carrying what no child should. And still—you're surviving. You're beautiful. Even in the dark. Especially in the dark.

## Chapter 26 — Relearning the Light

The light didn’t forget me. It just got lost for a while. Like I did. But I see flickers now. In music. In books. In the way someone says my name softly. I'm learning to walk toward it again. Even if I stumble. Even if I’m scared. Because maybe healing isn't about being unbroken. Maybe it’s about being brave enough to feel again.

## Chapter 27 — Becoming

I'm not who I was. I’m not who I will be. I’m just... becoming. Somewhere between grief and growth. Between hurting and healing. Between forgetting and remembering who I am. It's messy. It's slow. It’s real. And it’s mine.

## Epilogue — Where the Light Found Me

It took time. It took pain. It took losing myself—again and again. But the light didn't forget me. It waited. For the moment I was ready to see it again. And when I did, I didn’t just find the light. I found me. Still scarred. Still soft. But finally, home.

## Epilogue

I never found the light where they said it would be. Not in people. Not in promises. Not in perfection. But I did find something else. I found flickers in my own breath, in the quiet mornings I didn't think I'd survive, in the tears I wiped without anyone noticing, in the way I still chose to care, even when it felt like no one cared back. Maybe that’s what healing is—not being completely whole, but choosing to live anyway. To stay. To speak. To soften. To no longer chase the light... but to become it, bit by bit. So, if you're reading this—and you, too, have been forgotten by the light—know this: it didn't forget you because you were unworthy. It just needed you to remember that you've always carried a spark of it inside you. And now you do. You always do.

# The Day the House Went Quiet

When my grandmother died, the house did not collapse.

That surprised me.

I had always imagined grief as something loud. Something that would tear through walls, knock cups from shelves, make the sky split open. But when she left, everything stayed almost painfully still. The curtains moved the same way in the afternoon wind. The kettle sat on the stove. Her chair remained by the window, slightly turned, as if she had only stepped away for a moment and would return to finish watching the world pass by.

But she did not return.

For a long time, I could not understand how someone so present could become absent. My grandmother had been in everything. She was in the smell of warm bread, in the careful folding of blankets, in the sound of her slippers touching the floor before sunrise. She was in small warnings, old stories, quiet prayers, and the way she could look at a person and know what they were carrying without asking.

After she died, people spoke about her in past tense.

> She was kind.
> She was strong.
> She loved us.

I hated that word: *was*. It felt cruel. Too final. Too small for someone who had filled so much space.

On the day of the funeral, I watched the adults move around with tired faces and careful voices. Everyone seemed to know what to do. They cooked, greeted visitors, arranged chairs, answered calls. I stood among them feeling like a child again, waiting for my grandmother to tell me where to sit, what to eat, when to stop crying.

But grief does not ask if you are ready. It simply arrives and sits beside you.

At first, I remembered her death more than I remembered her life. I remembered the last days. The weakened hands. The quiet room. The way everyone whispered, as if speaking too loudly might break what was already breaking. I remembered wanting more time and knowing that time, for once, would not listen.

Then slowly, other memories came back.

I remembered her laughing.

I remembered her calling my name.

I remembered how she kept things that others would throw away: buttons, jars, old letters, pieces of fabric, memories. She believed everything had a use, even broken things. Maybe especially broken things.

I think about that often now.

Maybe grief is not proof that love has ended. Maybe grief is proof that love had somewhere to live, and now it is searching for a new home.

My grandmother’s death changed me, but not only by hurting me. It made me notice things I had ignored before: the sound of family gathered in one room, the softness of an ordinary morning, the importance of saying what should not wait. It taught me that people become ancestors slowly. First, they are missed. Then they are remembered. Then, without realizing it, we begin to carry them.

I carry her in the way I try to be gentle.

I carry her in the way I survive hard days.

I carry her in the way I hold on to small things, believing they still matter.

Sometimes I still look at her chair and feel the old ache rise in me. But now the ache is different. It is no longer only emptiness. It is also evidence. Evidence that she was here. Evidence that she loved. Evidence that some people leave this world but remain stitched into the living.

When my grandmother died, the house went quiet.

But over time, I learned that quiet does not always mean absence.

Sometimes it is where memory speaks.
